title: Coin-tape bound from a finite-message protocol
statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$. Fix real numbers $\varepsilon' < \varepsilon$, and suppose $p$ is a public-coin finite-message protocol with shared randomness $\Omega$ and private inputs in $X$ and $Y$ that $\varepsilon'$-computes $f$, meaning that for every input pair $(x,y)$ the probability over $\omega \in \Omega$ that the protocol's output differs from $f(x,y)$ is at most $\varepsilon'$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $f$ satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \;\le\; \mathrm{complexity}(p),
\]
where $\mathrm{complexity}(p)$ is the worst-case bit cost of $p$ (a $\beta$-valued message costing $\lceil \log_2 \abs{\beta}\rceil$ bits) and the inequality holds in $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω
p ε'-computes f (error at most ε' on every input)
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and $\varepsilon' < \varepsilon$.
If a finite-message public-coin protocol $p$ over $\Omega$ computes $f$ with error at most
$\varepsilon'$, then $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
This allows one to transfer upper bounds from protocols over arbitrary finite probability
spaces to the coin-tape formulation.
